summary.text: First named among the forty-four suitors from wooded Zacynthus in Apollodorus' island catalogue — wholly distinct from Eurylochus, Odysseus' companion who bound him to the mast when the Sirens sang.

story.text: Apollodorus opens the Zacynthian list with Eurylochus among the forty-four wooers who came from the island to devour Odysseus' house while the king was thought dead at Troy.

Homer's Eurylochus is a very different man — second in command among Odysseus' comrades, who urged landing on the Sun-god's cattle and helped bind his captain when the Sirens' song would have drawn him overboard. The Epitome name is a homonym hazard only.
